newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: International patent applications rose 21.6 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: International patent applications rose 21.6 percent in 1996.

text.p: The number of applications for international patents rose last year by 21.6 percent to 47,291, the World Intellectual Property Organisation said Friday.
American inventors and industrialists filed for 20,828, or 44 per cent, of the total, the organisation said.
Their rivals in Germany (5,695 or 12 per cent), Japan (3,861 or 8.2 per cent), Britain (3,440 or 7.3 per cent) and France (2,307 or 4.9 per cent) followed among the top five, it said.
The U.N. agency administers the 1978 Patent Cooperation Treaty, which facilitates obtaining patent protection for inventors and industry through filing a single international application.

Laurent Mandelier, a spokesman for the agency, said the treaty allows inventors and industrialists to file a request for an international patent covering up to 89 countries instead of filing 89 national requests.
